newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Australians got Holocaust money from SBC, not UBS.
newsitem.headline: Australians got Holocaust money from SBC, not UBS.

text.p: An Australian Jewish family who successfully claimed a dormant Holocaust account from a Swiss bank was dealing with Swiss Bank Corp (SBC), not Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), both institutes said on Wednesday.
Sydney accountant Stephen Baruch said at the weekend he made the deal three weeks ago in Zurich with UBS.
"The dormant account was at SBC," a UBS spoeksman told Reuters.
SBC, one of Switzerland's three big global banks alongside UBS and Credit Suisse Group, confirmed the deal but said a confidentialty pact with the Baruch family barred it from revealing details.
However, an SBC spokesman agreed with Baruch's statement that Australian news reports the account totalled around A$200,000 were "exaggerated".
Baruch said his grandfather, Salem Buzyner, deposited his money in a secret Swiss account to protect his family's assets from the Nazis during World War Two.
Buzyner died in Italy and his extended family moved to Australia.
Baruch said his personal case was successful because his family still held bank documents, which proved ownership of the funds.
